subject: ClearPath Medical — discovery recap, stakeholder map & internal exception ask
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T14:05:00Z
Subject: Post-call notes: ClearPath discovery — quick stakeholder map and asks

Team,

Quick recap from the 1:1 with Sarah Murphy (Head of Data) and Tom Chen (CTO) at ClearPath Medical — call ended ~30m ago. High level: they are evaluating Redwood for a 3-month pilot focused on summarization and routing of clinical intake forms. Key points below and immediate asks.

Highlights:
- Economic buyer: Tom Chen (CTO) — cares about TCO and integration effort.
- Security + procurement: procurement@clearpathmedical.com is the gate; they want SOC 2 + data residency notes; Sarah is coordinating.
- Decision criteria: accuracy on PHI redaction, latency under 400ms P95 for single-turn inference, and predictable cost for batch ingestion.

Immediate asks (from our side):
1) I attached a 1-page Mutual Action Plan that maps owners and timelines (ClearPath_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx). Please review.
2) Security exception: they asked for a specific SLA (99.5% with financial credit tiers) for an initial pilot. Dev, can you confirm feasibility and required compensating controls?
3) Commercial: they asked if we can do a pilot credit / discount (they’re budget-constrained) — thinking 20% pilot discount. Lauren/Marissa, what approval level do we need for that?

Next steps I propose:
- Ben to send post-call summary + MAP to Sarah + cc Tom and procurement.
- Lauren to confirm approval path for pilot discount and SLA exception.
- Dev to scope security asks and list required artifacts (SOC2, data flow diagram).

I’ll send the external follow-up now and loop you all in.

Ben
Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0142

Attachment: ClearPath_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call notes: ClearPath discovery — quick stakeholder map and asks

Thanks Ben — good call. A couple quick notes and asks from GTM/legal side: 

- Economic buyer confirmed: Tom Chen. Contract signer looks like VP of Finance once procurement finishes their review.
- For a pilot credit of ~20% we typically need manager approval + a finance notification; for anything >25% we escalate to Sales Ops. So 20% should be fine — I can approve but need a one-pager that lays out pilot scope and success metrics.
- SLA exception: we will need a short memo (1 paragraph) describing the ask (99.5% uptime + financial credits for pilot) and the business justification. Legal will triage after we clear security.

Marissa — can you draft the pilot scope/metrics (2 bullets: sample volume, duration, success metrics) and I’ll attach it to the approval memo.

Dev — can you confirm whether a temporary SLA variance for pilot-only is acceptable from Security? If yes, list the deliverables (SOC2 evidence, encryption at rest, network diagram) so I can route Legal/Finance.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the one-pager and Dev’s list.

Lauren
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Murphy <sarah.murphy@clearpathmedical.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@clearpathmedical.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T15:45:00Z
Subject: ClearPath next steps + mutual action plan (post-call)

Sarah / Tom — thanks again for your time just now. Short post-call summary and next steps (attached MAP).

Summary:
- Pilots: ClearPath is interested in a 3-month pilot for intake form summarization and routing.
- Success metrics: 85%+ accuracy on PHI redaction tests, P95 latency < 400ms for single-turn queries, and stable unit pricing for batch jobs.
- Timeline: ideally start onboarding in June, pilot in July.

Immediate asks for your team:
1) Please confirm the procurement contact and rough timeline. I have procurement@clearpathmedical.com listed — if there is a specific purchaser please share name + email.
2) Security artifacts: they asked for SOC 2 report and a short data flow diagram; Dev on my side will scope this.
3) Commercial: we can discuss a pilot discount — internally we are proposing 20% for the pilot to reduce friction. Lauren will follow up on approval path.

Attached: ClearPath_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (owners, dates, deliverables), and a draft SLA (SLA_draft_ClearPath_99_5.pdf) — note the SLA is a starting point for discussion.

If procurement has a standard questionnaire, please send it and I’ll make sure our security team gets the completed copy back to you within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Ben

---
Ben Carter | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-10T16:10:00Z
Subject: Re: ClearPath next steps + mutual action plan (post-call)

Ben / Lauren — quick security read. Thanks for the context.

What we can provide immediately:
- Latest SOC 2 Type II completion letter and control matrix (redacted) — I will attach to the Hub link once I confirm sharing policy.
- Data flow diagram for the pilot: we need to know whether they want on-prem connectors or SFTP push for PHI ingestion. If they push to our hosted API, we’ll require encryption in transit + at rest and explicit retention TTL for pilot data.

Regarding SLA exception:
- Pilot-only SLA variance to 99.5% is acceptable as a limited, non-binding commercial term, provided we include a rollback path and no long-term credits beyond the pilot.
- Required compensating controls: enforce mutual access logging, customer audit window (30 days), and an agreed incident notification timeline (30 mins for Sev1).

Deliverables needed from ClearPath to proceed on the security side:
1) Procurement questionnaire (or list of questions).
2) Contact for their internal security lead (name + email).
3) Confirmation of expected data transfer pattern (SFTP vs API).

If those items are provided, I can prepare a 1-page security memo and recommend the pilot SLA exception.

Dev
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:00:00Z
Subject: Approval request: pilot pricing + SLA/security exceptions for ClearPath (formal ask)

Lauren / Marissa — asking for formal approval to proceed with the following concessions for ClearPath pilot: 

Proposal (what we will offer to ClearPath for a 3-month pilot):
- Commercial: 20% pilot discount from list for pilot usage (pilot cap $12k).
- SLA: pilot-only SLA variance to 99.5% with non-recurring financial credits capped at 10% of pilot fees.
- Security: provide SOC 2 artifacts + 1-page security memo; require customer to use SFTP push with TTL on raw payloads (30 days).

Business justification:
- ClearPath is a mid-size regional health network with credible payer relationships; winning this pilot opens a path to enterprise rollout across 12 hospitals. Tom Chen is the economic buyer and is prepared to run a pilot quickly if procurement timeline is reasonable.
- Competitive position: they are evaluating three vendors; our combination of performance and observability is a differentiator.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: SLA credits and discount reduce short-term revenue. Mitigation: cap pilot to $12k and credits limited to 10% of pilot fees; require signed MOU before work begins.
- Risk: data residency/compliance. Mitigation: require SFTP with TTL + SOC 2 evidence; security memo will be explicit.

Requested approvals:
1) Lauren — approve the 20% pilot discount and MOU approach.
2) Marissa — confirm we can file this as a standard pilot SOW and route to Finance for accounting of the one-time discount.
3) Dev — please confirm you’ll produce the 1-page security memo within 48 hours of getting the procurement questionnaire.

If you approve, I will send a formal MOU with the terms and the mutual action plan to Sarah and Tom and attach the SLA draft.

Ben
Sales Lead | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: SLA_draft_ClearPath_99_5.pdf
